title: WITH: giving your subquery a name

steps.title: Name your table-on-the-fly
steps.prompt:
A CTE (say: 'see-tee-ee') is a subquery with a NAME, written at the top with WITH.
It's like sketching the plan on a napkin before writing the menu.
steps.task: Try typing: WITH busy AS (SELECT category_id, count(*) AS c FROM products GROUP BY category_id) SELECT * FROM busy WHERE c > 5;
hints: busy AS wraps the GROUP BY query.
Then a plain SELECT reads FROM busy.
Filter the named list with WHERE c > 5.
steps.expected_sql: WITH busy AS (SELECT category_id, count(*) AS c FROM products GROUP BY category_id) SELECT * FROM busy WHERE c > 5;
steps.memory_trick: WITH name AS (…) = 'here's a temporary list, call it this'.

steps.title: Fill the temporary name
steps.prompt:
Fill the blank with a name for the temporary list:
WITH ___ AS (SELECT category_id, count(*) AS c FROM products GROUP BY category_id) SELECT * FROM ___ WHERE c = 3;
steps.task: Use the same name in both blanks.
hints: The name is yours to invent.
Both blanks must hold the same word.
steps.expected_sql: WITH cheap AS (SELECT category_id, count(*) AS c FROM products GROUP BY category_id) SELECT * FROM cheap WHERE c = 3;
steps.seed_sql: WITH ___ AS (SELECT category_id, count(*) AS c FROM products GROUP BY category_id) SELECT * FROM ___ WHERE c = 3;
steps.memory_trick: Same name twice: once created, once used.

steps.title: Why bother with WITH?
steps.prompt:
WITH makes long questions readable: name the messy part once, use it after.
It also lets you reuse the same list later in the same query - no copy-paste.
steps.task: What is the temporary list called in SQL?
steps.memory_trick: CTE = a named napkin sketch you can reuse.
